notes: §1985:X.5.2.4 GR2: when the called program is made available control is transferred to it, and after its return 'the ON OVERFLOW or ON EXCEPTION phrase, if specified, is ignored and control is transferred to the end of the CALL statement or, if the NOT ON EXCEPTION phrase is specified, to imperative-statement-2', explicit transfers in imperative-statement-2 following their own rules. CallEmitter.EmitCall runs ProgramTable.CallProgram inside a catch that only an unsuccessful call reaches (EmitCallEcCatch), so a normal return skips imperative-statement-1 and EmitNotOnException runs imperative-statement-2 (2023's propagated-exception bypass needs 2002 RAISING/>>TURN, unreachable at 85); ConditionalPhrases.Associates/MayAssociate admit at 85 exactly Format 1's ON OVERFLOW or Format 2's [NOT] ON EXCEPTION. Probes: (b) NOT ON EXCEPTION with GO TO (leaves the CALL), with PERFORM plus a nested CALL ... END-CALL, ON OVERFLOW after a successful return (ignored), ON OVERFLOW with NOT ON EXCEPTION, NOT ON OVERFLOW, a repeated phrase (COBOL2269), an IF or READ without END- in imperative-statement-2 (COBOL2796) and an empty ON EXCEPTION (COBOL2072) refused; (e) a failed CALL takes ON EXCEPTION and skips NOT ON EXCEPTION. Unfiled lead outside this rule: NOT ON EXCEPTION written before ON EXCEPTION is accepted at 85 though §1985:IV.2.1 says optional elements 'must appear in the sequence shown' (pb3830_compute_zero_size_error pins the same reversal for SIZE ERROR at 85). The witness prints its eleven lines.

next.reason: 1985: when the program is made available 'control is transferred to the called program'; after return 'the ON OVERFLOW or ON EXCEPTION phrase, if specified, is ignored' and control goes to the end of the CALL or to imperative-statement-2. §2023:14.9.4.4 GR3g and GR3i keep this path ('the ON EXCEPTION phrase, if specified, is ignored ... control is transferred to the end of the CALL statement or, if the NOT ON EXCEPTION phrase is specified, to imperative-statement-2'), with explicit transfers per §2023:14.6.3 GR3. Two differences: ON OVERFLOW is gone (§2023:14.9.4.2 has only ON EXCEPTION, so a 1985 CALL ... ON OVERFLOW is refused), and 'If an exception condition is propagated from the called program, execution continues as specified in 14.6.13.1', bypassing NOT ON EXCEPTION.
